candidates.name: Event Tracing for Windows
verified_facts: Defines ETW providers, controllers, sessions, and consumers for high-performance event tracing.
semantic_limits: ETW is observational infrastructure; a trace must still be correlated to provider GUID, session, process, clock, and file identity.

candidates.name: StartTraceW
verified_facts: Registers and starts an ETW session and requires a unique descriptive session name and properties.
semantic_limits: ETW sessions are limited resources; this package documents the API and does not start a second session.

candidates.name: ControlTraceW
verified_facts: Queries, updates, flushes, or stops an ETW session according to the control code.
semantic_limits: Control operations mutate or affect live sessions and are not executed by this repository-only evidence package.

candidates.name: EnableTraceEx2
verified_facts: Enables or disables a provider for a trace session with level, keywords, properties, and optional filters.
semantic_limits: Provider enablement does not prove that expected events were emitted or that filters captured all relevant activity.

candidates.name: OpenTraceW
verified_facts: Opens a real-time session or ETL file for consumption and callback processing.
semantic_limits: Opening a trace does not establish source-file integrity, clock alignment, or provider authenticity.

candidates.name: ProcessTrace
verified_facts: Delivers trace events from one or more open trace handles to registered callbacks.
semantic_limits: Callback delivery order and loss indicators must be checked; processing alone is not gap-free proof.

candidates.name: CloseTrace
verified_facts: Closes a trace-consumer handle returned by OpenTrace.
semantic_limits: Handle closure is cleanup only and does not prove all buffered events were processed.

candidates.name: QueryAllTracesW
verified_facts: Retrieves properties for active event-tracing sessions visible to the caller.
semantic_limits: Session enumeration is security-context dependent and a matching name requires owner and configuration correlation.

candidates.name: EnumerateTraceGuidsEx
verified_facts: Enumerates registered providers or provider/session relationships for a selected information class.
semantic_limits: Registration or enablement does not prove event delivery or canonical runner ownership.

candidates.name: EVENT_TRACE_LOGFILEW
verified_facts: Configures ETW file or real-time consumption, callbacks, processing modes, and exposes loss counters.
semantic_limits: Loss counters, modes, timestamps, and logger identity must be read; the structure alone is not evidence.

candidates.name: EVENT_HEADER
verified_facts: Carries core ETW event identity including provider, descriptor, process, thread, timestamp, activity, and flags.
semantic_limits: Header identifiers can be reused or absent and must be joined to payload, session, clock, and process-start evidence.

candidates.name: EVENT_RECORD
verified_facts: Combines an ETW event header, buffer context, extended data, and user payload for consumer callbacks.
semantic_limits: Raw payload interpretation requires matching metadata and bounds checks; an event record is not self-describing proof.

candidates.name: Trace Data Helper overview
verified_facts: Describes TDH-based decoding of manifest, MOF, WPP, and TraceLogging event metadata and properties.
semantic_limits: TDH decoding depends on available metadata and does not authenticate the producer or trace file.
